title: Billing a Retiree Enrolled under More Than One Sponsor in the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
Where a retiree holds enrollments under more than one sponsor, each is billed on its own group contract and the balances are never pooled.

## Money that arrives without a group reference

Money arriving without a group reference is applied to the oldest unpaid coverage month across the retiree's enrollments, and the retiree is told which enrollment it was applied to.

## Money remitted by a sponsor in bulk

A sponsor's bulk remittance is split across the retirees it names and never applied to a retiree the sponsor did not name, however obvious the intention seems.

## Two sponsors covering the same month

Where a retiree is enrolled under two sponsors for the same coverage month, the plan tells them plainly that only one plan pays as primary and helps them end the other.

## What the retiree pays in the month

A retiree's total monthly contribution is the sum of what each sponsor set, and no cap applies across sponsors because each group contract stands alone. The monthly share each sponsor set is taken from that sponsor's own enrollment, and the total is what those shares come to together; there is no figure at which the total stops.

## Points of judgement

| Question put to the records | What governs |
| --- | --- |
| Which balance does a charge belong to | The group contract of the enrollment charged, since balances are never pooled |
| Where does unreferenced money go | The oldest unpaid coverage month across the retiree's enrollments |
| May a bulk remittance reach a retiree the file omits | No, however plainly the sponsor seems to have meant it |
| Is there a ceiling on the retiree's total monthly contribution | No, because each group contract stands alone |

The figures that make up each side of a month's premium on a given plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans are the total group premium for that plan, the default retiree contribution and the default sponsor share scheduled for it.
